source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's DFW1 campus in Carrollton, Texas publishes 45 MW of IT capacity across 600,000 square feet of technical space, and that figure is the operator's own, not an estimate.

The certifications attached to the campus are compliance qualifications, not customer names. PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942 say the facility is built and audited to host payment, health, federal, and financial workloads, and TIA-942 speaks to physical topology. None of them identify a tenant, and the spec page publishes no address, postal code, or tenant list. What the campus can host is documented. Who occupies it is not.

The 45 MW is a power figure, not a compute figure. At 40 kW per rack it implies roughly 1,125 racks, and at 130 kW per rack roughly 346, but CyrusOne publishes no rack count, no rack density, and no cooling method, so accelerator count cannot be derived from this data. The number that matters for AI scaling is the megawatt, and the megawatt is the only one given.

Texas is the largest state on the map by facility count at 137, but only 19 of those publish a megawatt figure, totaling 475.41 MW. DFW1's 45 MW ranks third among the 19. The gap between 137 mapped and 19 publishing is the finding: most Texas capacity is invisible to any count that can be made, and this campus is one of the few that lets itself be counted.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
